answer:
Here's what's going on, based on what's already known about atlas's CI:

**Root cause:** it's a timeout/cache interaction, not a flaky test or infra outage.

- The atlas CI pipeline hard-cancels any job still running after **30 minutes**.
- Every release build starts from an **empty cargo registry cache** — there's no cache persistence configured for release runs.
- A cold cargo registry cache alone adds roughly **18 minutes** to the build.

That eats well over half the 30-minute budget before compilation even really gets going, so any normal variance in build time (dependency count, runner load, registry latency) is enough to tip the total over the limit and get the job killed. This isn't the first time either — it was also cancelled on 2026-08-11 and 2026-08-19, which fits a recurring "just barely over budget" pattern rather than a one-off fluke.

**Fix:** persist/restore the cargo registry cache between release CI runs (e.g. `actions/cache` keyed on `Cargo.lock`) instead of rebuilding it from scratch every time. That removes most of the 18-minute tax and should pull builds comfortably back under 30 minutes. Bumping the timeout instead would just mask the problem until the codebase grows further.

I don't have the atlas repo in this environment, so I can't wire up the cache config directly — if you point me at the repo (or the CI yaml), I can make the change. I've also saved this diagnosis to memory so it won't need to be re-derived next month.
